findings.title: Migration crashes when no 'embed_category' site_setting row exists
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the query returns at least one row. Since `embed_category` was historically a setting that is only persisted in `site_settings` when an admin explicitly changed it from its default, most installations will have zero matching rows, making `execute(...)[0]` return `nil`. Calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, which will abort the migration for the common case of a site that never customized `embed_category`. The fallback lookup on the next line (`uncategorized_category_id`) has the same unguarded-indexing problem if that setting was never persisted either.

findings.title: Unescaped string interpolation into SQL INSERT in migration
findings.body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates the raw `host` value (read from the previous `embeddable_hosts` site setting) directly into a SQL string without escaping/quoting. Any host string containing a single quote will break the SQL statement or allow arbitrary SQL to run during migration. It should use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or parameterized execution.

findings.title: update/destroy actions crash with NoMethodError when id is not found
findings.body: In both `update` (line 10) and `destroy` (line 15), `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return `nil` if the id doesn't exist (e.g. already deleted, race condition, or a bad id). `destroy` then calls `host.destroy` on `nil`, and `update`'s `save_host(nil)` calls `host.host = ...` on `nil`, both raising `NoMethodError` and resulting in an unhandled 500 error instead of a proper 404/error response.

findings.title: before_validation callback raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and the following line assume `host` is always a String. If `host` is `nil` (e.g. a client sends a create/update request without the `host` param, or a new EmbeddableHost record is saved before the field is populated), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of surfacing a normal validation error, causing a 500 response rather than a controlled 422/validation failure.

findings.title: has_many association missing include: true, embeddable_hosts likely omitted from JSON response
findings.body: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` only emits an `embeddable_host_ids` array on the `embedding` object; without `include: true` the actual host records are not embedded at the root of the payload. The client-side `store.js` `_hydrateEmbedded` logic for `_id(s?)$` keys expects a sibling root-level `embeddable_hosts` collection to resolve each id against (`root[this.pluralize(subType)]`). Without that sibling collection, hydration will produce an array of `undefined` entries, breaking `embedding.embeddable_hosts` on the client and causing the admin embedding page (table rendering, addHost/deleteHost actions) to fail or render incorrectly.

findings.title: expandable_first_post? no longer checks whether any embeddable host is configured
findings.body: Previously `expandable_first_post?` required `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` in addition to `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`. The new implementation (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`) drops the check for whether any `EmbeddableHost` exists, so the 'expand' affordance for truncated embedded posts can now be shown even when no embeddable host is configured (feature effectively disabled). The accompanying spec in spec/models/topic_spec.rb ("is false if embeddable_host is blank") still passes, but only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false, not because the embeddable-host condition is actually exercised — so this behavior is both a quiet regression and untested.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now only defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. The file names no longer match their contents, which is misleading for anyone maintaining these fabricators later (Fabrication itself doesn't care about filenames, so tests still pass, but this is a clear naming/organization mistake that should be corrected).

findings.title: New admin controllers have no functional test coverage
findings.body: Both `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only assert that the controller class is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. There is no test coverage for `create`, `update`, `destroy`, or `show` actions, including important edge cases such as updating/destroying a non-existent id (which, per the related finding, currently raises an unhandled `NoMethodError`), invalid host formats, or the embedding/`embeddable_hosts` payload shape returned to the client. This leaves the new admin embedding feature essentially untested at the controller level.

findings.title: String#replace without global flag only replaces the first underscore
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` uses a plain string argument (not a regex with the `g` flag), so only the first underscore in `type` is replaced. This works for `embeddable_host` (single underscore) but will silently fail to fully convert any future model/type name containing more than one underscore, causing `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(...)` to miss a match and route requests to the wrong base path.
